The more I practice the more I see FO and EG as the same thing...the only difference is scale & time.

Here is an example:

Look at the area is red:

NZD-USD Weekly

Clearly this is a FO, and if you saw it as an engulf in 2001 you probably lost some money

For the purposes of this scale though, it's a FO.

Here is the uncompleted FL Box for this PA:

The low is set....bu the highs of the FL Box are not set until a new low is made (engulf). Then any break above the 'set' highs is a FO.

You can't determine if a break above the highs is a FO until you confirm an engulf has occurred below. Until a new low occurs, this is an incomplete FL Box.

Although this is a very HTF example, this exact same concept occurs over and over again in every scale.

If you refer back to Salivan's post on my journal (#1306) you will see a chart he edited for me. I am posting it below for quick reference. You can see he is referring to the same concept...The FO can't be confirmed until a new low engulfs the old to completed the FL Box in this scale. This how to keep the FO vs. EG straight.

1. Know your scale 2. Know your important completed FL Boxes 3. Be carefully watching incomplete FL Boxes 4. Know ahead of time what your target will be for a valid engulf 5. Know ahead of time where your MPL is for a confirmed FO

And here is a nested (fractal) incomplete FL Box located within Incomplete FL Box 1.

Also, it seems like there are two types of engulfs...continuation engulfs and reversal engulfs.

Here is a close up. I know the chart is messy (sorry ) but I want to label all the important parts for those who are trying to learn too. It looks confusing but it is just a FL Box with a FO to a different FL, and a RT to a QM level.

I notice price came within a few pips of hitting its intended target before reversing back to the QM level. The target was an ORFL, so this wasn't unexpected, but it can be confusing to traders who assume the target was already reached and look at the RT to the QM level as a reversal to a lower FL (they see the original FO as an engulf and get in on the wrong side of the trade).

In previous posts, Salivan has mentioned the issue of price faking out to a different FL. I think this is important, and I notice many of the successful QM trades occur in situations where price forms the initial 'shoulder' of the QM by engulfing a swap zone (originally formed FL, not a reactive FL), and forms a FO past the newly formed MPL in to a FL above/below.

I will spend some time researching this tomorrow, as it may be an important piece of the puzzle.

This helps with determining FO vs. EG as well...scale is always a consideration.

Often, I see multiple FL Boxes all in close proximity to each other. Sometimes they overlap.

For example, here is a EUR-GBP chart.

FL Box 3 is important...price breaks the low but cannot sustain the break. We essentially have a FO (on this scale). The origin up is Box 4.

...but then we are faced with a decision to make regarding the importance of FL Box 5 and 6. Which one is more important?

Fl Box 5 is formed when price engulfs the top of FL Box 3. FL Box 6 is formed when price engulfs FL Box 2.

These two boxes overlap each other...

When price returns to this are of overlap, the PA will get confusing regarding EG and FO and MPL.

My opinion is that FL Box 5 is most important because it occurred first, and it held price above FL Box 3 which was temporarily breached by an unsustained FO to the downside. Fl Box 5 represents confirmed Bullish control (swap zone).

I will focus on these two engulfs next:

Here is FL Box 5 and FL Box 6...there is a substantial area of overlap between these.

Is the FTR of FL Box 5 a god candidate for a FO since it is formed below FL Box 6? The more important EG occurs in FL Box 5.

Would it be safest to wait for price to FO to the MPL of FL Box 5 since it was formed before FL Box 6 and is more important?

Another good example of a QM FO to a different FL.

I still don't understand exactly why price turns at these levels, but with more practice I assume I'll recognize a pattern.

I notice its important to closely look at the FO and draw all the LTF FL Boxes (DP to FO, EG of DP to FO etc...) because often times price turns just before the actual QM level (as is the case in this example) because price turns where the FOF is located.

Here is a HTF View:

And here is a LTF view of the exact entry. I extended the lime green line to identify where price turned. As you can see, it turned at the first area of FOF formed after the trick/FO....very close to the QM level (but missing it by a few pips). This trade would have ~ 10 pip stop and over 250 pip limit. Amazing R:R.

I do notice the FO of important FL Boxes occurs within the scope of a much larger confirmed FL Box... a bearish controlled FL Box. Probably a good idea to trade in the direction of the larger FL Box your PA is located within...

I notice the QM level is a DP to EG the large FL Box...this is the EG that confirms the HTF FL Box (without the LL the box is not confirmed). Also, you can see how scale helps to refine the actual FL...the LTF FL is where price reacts, the FO occurs in to a different FL. The higher time frame FL Box includes the FO as part of the FL Box, but that is the wrong scale for this QM trade.

The DP to EG is also a higher time frame FL Box (the yellow shaded portion is a more refined LTF FL). This higher time frame FL Box has the same three decision points as the much larger FL Box has....

1. Engulf 2. RT 3. New Low

What is the significance of the location of FO? I don't see it...
